sections.h2: Where is Florence, SC, and how is the city laid out?
sections.html:
Florence is the county seat of Florence County, in the northeastern part of South Carolina's coastal plain. It sits where Interstate 20 ends and Interstate 95 passes through. The 2020 census counted 39,899 people inside roughly 23.5 square miles, which made it the tenth most populous city in the state.

Jeffries Creek runs south of the center and drains toward the Great Pee Dee River. The Timrod Park area, known for older homes, was folded into the downtown redevelopment district, a program that began in 2010 and covers about 500 acres. If your house is on one of the older streets near downtown, its age is part of the story a buyer will want to hear.

sections.h2: How did Florence get its start?
sections.html:
Florence grew up around a railroad junction. The city was named for Florence Harllee, daughter of Gen. William Harllee, who led the Wilmington and Manchester Railroad and built his home at the point where lines met.

Three lines came together here: the Wilmington and Manchester, the Northeastern, and the Cheraw and Darlington. Florence County was created in 1888, and the town was incorporated in December 1890. The city was named an All-America City in 1965. That rail history explains the street grid and the older commercial blocks, and it explains why so many routes still cross here today.

sections.h2: What do people in Florence do for work?
sections.html:
Healthcare is the largest part of the Florence economy. McLeod Regional Medical Center is a 453-bed nonprofit hospital, and MUSC Florence has 420 beds. Between them they are described as the first and third largest employers in the Pee Dee region.

Manufacturing and corporate operations add to that base. The city's entry lists GE Healthcare (MRI manufacturing), Patheon (pharmaceutical manufacturing), Otis Elevator, a QVC distribution operation, TRICARE regional operations, Assurant, and offices of banks and rail and utility companies. Higher education adds Francis Marion University and Florence-Darlington Technical College.

For a seller, a mix like this means the people who might want your house are not tied to one employer. A nurse, a plant technician and a university employee all look at the same neighborhood differently, and each of them cares about different repairs.

sections.h2: How do you get around Florence and the Pee Dee?
sections.html:
Two interstates meet at Florence, and the distances below are the ones given for the city's highway connections.

  • I-95 runs northeast about 87 miles to Fayetteville, NC, and southwest about 179 miles to Savannah, GA.
  • I-20 runs west about 83 miles to Columbia.
  • US 52, US 76 and US 301 also pass through the area.
  • Florence Regional Airport (FLO) is about two miles east of downtown on US 76 and has American Eagle service to Charlotte.
  • Amtrak's Palmetto and Silver Meteor stop in the city.
  • The local bus system, PDRTA, has been free to ride since August 11, 2025.

Florence Public School District One runs 20 schools (13 elementary, 4 middle and 3 high schools), and several private schools operate in the city. Ask your agent or the district office which school zone a specific address falls in before you quote it to a buyer.

sections.h2: What does Florence's weather mean for a house?
sections.html:
Florence has a humid subtropical climate, so air conditioning and roofing take the most wear. The average July high is 92.9 degrees, the average January high is 56.9, and the record high is 108. The city gets about 48 inches of precipitation a year on roughly 118 days.

Hurricane Florence (September 2018) is the storm local buyers remember. The State Climatology Office reports that the Pee Dee River at Pee Dee crested at 31.83 feet, about a foot and a half below its 1945 record, and that drought before the storm held the flooding down. Floodwater from North Carolina moved slowly through the Yadkin-Pee Dee watershed, so high water lingered across the region.

Practical points if you are selling:

  • Gather roof, HVAC and water heater dates, since heat and humidity shorten their lives.
  • Keep any flood or water damage records and repair receipts together.
  • Expect buyers and lenders to ask about flood insurance, so find your current policy details.
  • Photograph standing water, crawlspace conditions and drainage after a hard rain, if you can.

sections.h2: How is property tax billed and paid on a Florence house?
sections.html:
Florence County bills real estate tax once a year, and the Florence County Treasurer collects it. According to the City of Florence, the city sets its millage by June 30 for a July 1 fiscal year, and the current city rate is $54.90 per $1,000 of assessed value. County and school levies come on top of that.

A qualifying owner-occupied home is assessed at 4 percent of market value. Rental and business real property is assessed at 6 percent. Real property is reappraised every five years, with notices usually mailed around May.

The city's tax payment page lists the Treasurer at 843-665-3041, the Tax Assessor at 843-665-3056 and the delinquent tax office at 843-665-3095. Delinquent real property and mobile homes can be sold at a public sale run by the county. If you owe back taxes on a house you want to sell, the balance will be paid from the proceeds at closing, so get a payoff figure early.

sections.h2: What steps does a Florence home sale follow under South Carolina law?
sections.html:
A South Carolina attorney has to be involved in the closing. The state Supreme Court has treated preparing deeds, examining title, overseeing closings and disbursing loan proceeds as the practice of law, as explained in Boone v. Quicken Loans (2017).

The deed is recorded at the Florence County Register of Deeds, 180 N. Irby Street, phone 843-665-3032. That office records deeds, plats and mortgages, but it does not prepare deeds, run title searches or give legal advice. Its county page links a fee sheet and an online search.

The state deed recording fee is $1.85 for realty valued at $100 to $500, plus $1.30 for each additional $500, according to the Department of Revenue.

Sellers also owe the buyer a written property condition disclosure statement before a contract is signed, unless the sale is exempt. Under the state code, exempt transfers include those by a fiduciary of an estate, trust or conservatorship, court-ordered sales, transfers to a spouse or lineal relatives, and sales where both parties agree in writing to skip the form. If something in the form changes before closing, the owner has to correct it or make reasonable repairs.

sections.h2: What permit and code rules apply to Florence houses?
sections.html:
The City of Florence Building and Permitting Department, at 324 West Evans Street, issues permits for construction, additions and remodeling. Its phone is 843-665-3151, and it is open weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Applications and inspection requests go through the city's online self-service portal.

The city has adopted the 2021 International Property Maintenance Code along with the 2021 residential and building codes. That matters if a house has been vacant, because a code officer can cite a property for conditions that a buyer would never see in a listing photo. Work done without a permit is something to raise with a buyer up front. A call to the department with your address is a quick way to find out what the city has on file.

Fees and permit triggers are not listed on the department page, so ask the office before you start a repair or sign a contract that depends on one.

sections.h2: What do Florence sellers usually run into?
sections.html:
The situations we hear about most in Florence are inherited houses, rentals with tenants, homes that need roof or HVAC work, and owners who have fallen behind on payments or taxes. Each one has a Florence-specific wrinkle.

  • Inherited homes: a sale by an estate representative is generally exempt from the state disclosure form, but the deed still has to be recorded and an attorney still handles the closing.
  • Rentals: the county assesses rental property at 6 percent rather than 4, and a former owner-occupant should confirm the status of any legal residence credit with the Tax Assessor.
  • Tax arrears: after the penalty dates above, unpaid real property can be sold at a county public sale.
  • Older homes near downtown: expect questions about the roof, wiring and plumbing, and gather any permit records.

A cash buyer can purchase a Florence house as is, and the closing still runs through a South Carolina attorney and the Register of Deeds. Compare any offer against what you would net after repairs, tax proration and the time a listing could take.

faqs.q: Do I need an attorney to sell a house in Florence, SC?
faqs.a: Yes, in practice. South Carolina treats deed preparation, title examination and closing supervision as the practice of law, so a licensed South Carolina attorney handles the closing. The deed is then recorded at the Florence County Register of Deeds.

faqs.q: When are Florence property taxes due?
faqs.a: January 15 each year, or the next business day if that date falls on a weekend or holiday. Penalties start on January 16 at 3 percent and reach 15 percent after March 17, according to the City of Florence.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Florence County?
faqs.a: At the Register of Deeds, 180 N. Irby Street, Florence, SC 29501. The office phone is 843-665-3032. It records deeds and mortgages but does not prepare deeds or give legal advice.

faqs.q: Did Hurricane Florence flood the city of Florence?
faqs.a: The State Climatology Office reports prolonged river flooding across the Pee Dee region in 2018, with the Pee Dee River cresting at 31.83 feet at Pee Dee. It does not break out city of Florence flooding, so check a specific address with the county and your insurer.

faqs.q: Can I sell an inherited house in Florence without a disclosure form?
faqs.a: Often yes. South Carolina exempts transfers by fiduciaries who administer a decedent's estate from the property condition disclosure requirement. Confirm the details with your closing attorney, because the exemption depends on who is signing the deed.
